s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented skin lesions with gradual coalescence and absence of hair growth
salient_findings: Multiple round, hypopigmented macules on face and neck
Lesions symmetrically distributed and ranging from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
key_facts: 2-year history of skin lesions
Lesions are asymptomatic
Lesions are round and hypopigmented
Lesions are symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions have coalesced over time
No hair growth at the site of the lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings show plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consist of clear/pale epithelial cells with glycogen accumulation
Stroma is formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules with absence of hair growth

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by multiple, round, hypopigmented macules, consistent with the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Pityriasis alba
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with hypopigmented patches, often on the face, although the lack of scaling and the presence of elastosis make it less likely

shortlist.label: Morpheaform basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords and marked elastosis are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Nevus sebaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with hypopigmented macules and absence of hair growth, although the histopathologic features are not entirely consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with neoplastic cords consisting of clear/pale epithelial cells and marked elastosis in the dermis surrounding the tumor are characteristic of Nevus sebaceus. The clinical presentation of asymptomatic, round, hypopigmented macules that are symmetrically distributed on the face and neck also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: Lack of histopathologic findings characteristic of Nevus depigmentosus

rejected.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with multiple small, discrete, hypopigmented macules, not coalescing lesions

rejected.label: Pityriasis alba
rejected.why: Usually presents with ill-defined, faintly hypopigmented patches and scaling, not characteristic of the described lesions

rejected.label: Morpheaform basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents as a solitary, indurated, and sometimes pigmented plaque, not multiple coalescing macules
